Quick answer US and Canada: most policies we checked reimburse care at any licensed vet in the US, and most also in Canada (some only during a temporary stay). Lemonade covers the US only. Outside the US and Canada: only Embrace and Nationwide say their policies cover vet care abroad. The rest limit cover to the US (and usually Canada), sometimes adding US territories or military bases, or their sites don’t say (marked “Check” in the table). Waiting periods: illness cover usually starts only after a waiting period of up to 30 days (14 or 15 days at most insurers we checked), so a policy bought the week before a trip may not cover that trip. Pre-existing conditions are generally not covered, and that includes anything that first shows up during a waiting period. You pay first: pet insurance usually reimburses you after you pay the vet, so budget for the full bill on the road. Policies differ by state, product and underwriting company, and insurers change

Korea’s import rules come from the Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency (APQA); USDA APHIS endorses the US health certificate. Book the rabies antibody (FAVN) test early: the result has to be on the health certificate. Quick answer Dogs and cats 90 days or older from the US: ISO 11784/11785 microchip, current rabies vaccination given before arrival, and a rabies-neutralizing antibody (FAVN) result of 0.5 IU/ml or more from an internationally approved lab, with the blood drawn within 24 months. If everything checks out, the pet can be released on the day of arrival. Source Paperwork: A health certificate issued by a USDA-accredited vet and endorsed by USDA APHIS within 30 days of export. The vet can submit it through VEHCS, but APHIS must ink-sign and emboss it, and the original must travel with your pet. Source Puppies and kittens under 90 days: No rabies vaccination or antibody test needed, but they still need an ISO microchip and a certificate showing the chip number and birth date. Source Advance notice: Only needed when you bring 10 or more dogs and/or cats: send APQA an advance notification and get approval for a quarantine facility first. Source If something is missing: No microchip, a chip number that doesn't match, no antibody test or a result under 0.5 IU/ml: the pet is held in quarantine at your expense (APQA says 10 days on average, sometimes longer). pages.b: Travelling with a dog or cat between the USA and Canada Personal pets moving between the United States and Canada usually need only a valid rabies certificate to enter Canada, and the free CDC Dog Import Form (plus age and microchip rules) to return to the United States. Always confirm with CFIA and CDC before you travel. Quick answer Official rule Dogs older than 8 months and cats entering Canada as personal pets: a current rabies vaccination certificate from a licensed vet (English or French, identifying the animal) is enough. No USDA APHIS health-certificate endorsement is required for these cases. Source Checked Nov 9, 2026 Official rule Dogs 3–8 months travelling with their owner: rabies certificate if 3 months or older. Dogs under 3 months: no rabies vaccine required, but carry proof of age. Source Checked Nov 9, 2026 Official rule Unaccompanied dogs under 8 months: health certificate issued by a licensed US vet within 72 hours of arrival in Canada; APHIS endorsement is not required for that certificate. Source Checked Nov 9, 2026 Official rule Return to the US (dogs): Canada is not on the CDC high-risk dog-rabies list. Every dog needs the free CDC Dog Import Form receipt, must be 6 months or older, microchipped, and look healthy. The same receipt can be reused for 6 months for US↔Canada trips if the dog visits no other country. Source Checked Nov 9, 2026 Official rule Cats returning to the US: no federal rabies proof or USDA health certificate required; the cat must appear healthy. State and airline rules still apply. pages.b: Travelling with a dog or cat between the USA and Mexico Since 3 August 2026, US-origin dogs need a New World screwworm (NWS) inspection certificate signed by a USDA-accredited vet within 5 days of entry into Mexico (no APHIS endorsement). Cats still need no health certificate. Returning dogs also need a SENASICA screwworm-freedom certificate plus the CDC Dog Import Form. Quick answer Official rule Dogs US → Mexico (since 3 Aug 2026): NWS Inspection Certificate for Pet Dogs Moving from the US to Mexico, signed by a USDA-accredited veterinarian within 5 days before entry. No APHIS endorsement. Missing or improper NWS paperwork can mean denied entry or holding at the border. Source Checked Nov 9, 2026 Official rule Cats US → Mexico: no health certificate and no NWS document since 16 Dec 2019. Do not add cats to the dog NWS form — that invalidates it. Source Checked Nov 9, 2026 Official rule At Mexico OISA (SENASICA): pet must show no disease signs, no ectoparasites, no fresh/healing wounds. Dirty bedding, toys and extra food are removed/destroyed; only that day’s food ration is allowed. Source Checked Nov 9, 2026 Official rule Return dogs Mexico → US: Mexico has been screwworm-affected since 22 Nov 2024. Every dog needs a screwworm-freedom certificate from a SENASICA-approved vet (inspection ≤5 days before travel) PLUS CDC Dog Import Form, age ≥6 months, microchip, healthy appearance. Source Checked Nov 9, 2026 Official rule Mexico is not on the CDC high-risk dog-rabies list (low-risk for CDC rabies rules). Screwworm rules are separate USDA/SENASICA requirements. Pets may not travel in the cabin on commercial flights into GB; use an approved route. Returning to the US follows CDC low-risk rules.
